discretion.description: The only contentions shown concern standing; the appellant argued the project obstructs a scenic vista (the panoramic view from Route 15) protected by the regulations and plans, and raised traffic effects, but the merits grounds of the appeal are not otherwise set out.

observed_status.description: The appeal was dismissed for the appellant's lack of standing, leaving the Planning Commission's final plan approval in place; nothing is shown pending.

judgments.note: Appeal of a Planning Commission final plan approval for a new 48-unit congregate housing facility (a residence), so municipal appeal and new housing are both yes.

The appeal was dismissed on standing before any merits hearing; the evidentiary hearing was on standing only and 24 V.S.A. 4471 is cited only for participation, so neither on-the-record nor de novo review is established.
End is the 2006-09-25 dismissal concluding the appeal; no filing date or earlier dated event appears, so start is unknown and kind/days are unknown.
Relationship coded other: Post is a town resident 0.9 miles away whom the court found not in the immediate neighborhood; she claimed to represent Essex citizens generally. Neighbor is arguable.
Only standing arguments are described; the scenic-vista argument suggests an evaluative merits contention but the appeal's merits grounds and tests are not set out.
Dismissal leaves the Planning Commission's final plan approval standing; whether it carried conditions is not stated, so allowed rather than allowed_with_conditions.
The date of the Planning Commission decision is not stated.
